plastic_detail: Plastic is waste we use almost every day, such as drinking bottles, iced coffee cups, food containers, snack boxes, or bottle caps. Many people think that once used, it's done but in reality, plastic has great value. If properly sorted, it can be recycled into new products such as textile fibers, trash bins, tables and chairs, or new packaging. Additionally, some types of plastic can be processed into fuel or oil through technologies like pyrolysis, helping reduce accumulated waste. Before disposal, pour out any liquids or food residue, rinse lightly, and flatten the item to make storage and recycling easier.
paper_detail: Paper is a material that is easy to use and can be reused many times, such as office paper, books, notebooks, cardboard boxes, shipping boxes, or paper bags. If kept clean and dry, it can be recycled by factories into new paper sheets, corrugated boxes, or tissue paper. Separating paper helps reduce tree cutting and conserves natural resources. Before discarding, fold it neatly and keep it separate from wet waste to prevent damage that would make it unrecyclable.
metal_detail: Metal is a high-value waste material that can be recycled very efficiently, such as soda cans, coffee cans, bottle caps, or aluminum scraps. When separated from general waste, it can be melted down and remanufactured into new cans, electronic components, or construction materials multiple times. A key advantage of metal is that it can be recycled repeatedly while maintaining its quality. Before disposal, rinse off any food or drink residue for cleanliness and easier sorting.
glass_detail: Glass is a durable material that can be recycled efficiently, such as juice bottles, sauce bottles, beverage bottles, perfume bottles, or other glass containers. When melted down, it can be made into new bottles or containers while maintaining its original quality. Separating glass helps reduce the use of new raw materials and lowers energy consumption in production. However, glass breaks easily—if it is broken, it should be wrapped or placed in a separate bag before disposal to ensure the safety of others and waste collection workers.
